key_insight: Pretraining codec-avatar models at very large scale (millions of samples) substantially closes the gap between studio-level fidelity and in-the-wild generalization, enabling high-quality, controllable avatars that transfer well to real-world data.
problem_solved: Addresses the fidelity-versus-generalization trade-off: studio multi-view captures yield precise, controllable avatars but don’t generalize, while existing large-scale in-the-wild models generalize but lack studio-grade detail; large-scale avatar pretraining delivers both.
method: Assemble and pretrain a codec-avatar model on a massive, diverse dataset combining in-the-wild and studio-like samples to learn robust, high-capacity representations.
Use a compact codec-avatar representation that supports high-fidelity reconstruction and parameterized control (expressions/pose) while being amenable to large-scale learning.
Transfer or fine-tune the pretrained model to studio subjects to recover precise, controllable avatars with improved real-world robustness and reduced per-subject capture needs.
impact: Enables scalable creation of high-quality, controllable avatars without heavy reliance on costly studio capture; useful for VR/AR, telepresence, and downstream vision/graphics tasks where both fidelity and generalization matter.
visual_elements: Trade-off diagram: fidelity (studio) vs generalization (in-the-wild) showing how large-scale pretraining moves the model toward the Pareto front.
Pipeline flowchart: data collection (studio + in-the-wild) → large-scale pretraining → fine-tuning/deployment.
Scaling curve: performance (reconstruction quality/generalization) vs dataset size highlighting ‘unreasonable effectiveness’ of scale.
Qualitative panel: side-by-side avatar renders—studio-only model, in-the-wild-only model, and pretrained+fine-tuned model.
paper_title: Large-scale Codec Avatars: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Large-scale Avatar Pretraining
paper_authors: Junxuan Li, Rawal Khirodkar, Chengan He, Zhongshi Jiang, Giljoo Nam
